_note: 粉もの（小麦粉の生地を鉄板・銅板で焼くもの）の系譜。品目ハブ（/en/eat/konamono/）の横並び表と、各系譜ページがここから描く。出典は docs/research/konamono-2026-10-10.md と各系譜ページの sources。お好み焼きは大阪と広島を1ページ、たこ焼きと明石焼を1ページにまとめた。もんじゃはメモに素材が無いので planned
name: Konamono (batter dishes)

lineages.name: Okonomiyaki (Osaka and Hiroshima)
lineages.nameJa: お好み焼き（大阪・広島）

origin.era: prewar snacks; present forms postwar, Hiroshima's name c. 1950

cells.batter: Osaka: flour and dashi, often with grated yam, cabbage mixed in. Hiroshima: a thin crêpe of batter
cells.cooked: Osaka: mixed and grilled. Hiroshima: layered — cabbage, pork, noodles and egg stacked and steamed
cells.howToEat: Osaka: sometimes as a side with rice. Hiroshima: with noodles, not rice, eaten with a spatula or chopsticks

lineages.name: Takoyaki and Akashi-yaki
lineages.nameJa: たこ焼き・明石焼（玉子焼）

origin.era: Osaka: early Shōwa stalls. Akashi: shop trade said to date from 1919

cells.batter: Takoyaki: flour, dashi, egg. Akashi: more egg, plus wheat starch (jinko), so it stays soft
cells.cooked: Takoyaki: a takoyaki pan at about 220°C, turned 90° at a time into balls. Akashi: copper pan
cells.finish: Takoyaki: thick sauce, green laver, bonito flakes. Akashi: none — dipped in dashi
cells.howToEat: Takoyaki: from a boat-shaped tray with a toothpick. Akashi: on a wooden board (age-ita), 20 to a portion at one old shop
